Senses.Explanation: A discourse opener that raises the one matter at stake and hands it straight to a concrete image: a fire-mass, a boat poling upstream, a man up a tree, a general taking the field. Song and Yuan openers set the shape: Yuanwu Keqin rules in his case commentary that this matter does not live in word and phrase, or the whole canon would have sufficed and the First Patriarch's crossing would have been needless; Gaofeng Yuanmiao opens with the image of a great fire-mass whose blaze leaves no gap, where everything in the world melts like a snowflake on contact; Tianyin Yuanxiu raises it at an evening assembly with his staff in hand, ruling that seasoned adepts know it before it is raised while newer arrivals must still strive. Later records keep the opening hinge and keep feeding it images: Guxue Zhenzhe likens it at an evening assembly to a wildfire on the mountains that one wind-blown spark reduces to ash across a thousand peaks; Baiyu Jingsi opens the address greeting a newly cast cloud plate with the casting itself, dross melted away in the great furnace; Yushan Shangsi opens a raised seat with the man up the tree, mouth holding the branch, no hand to climb and no foot to stand; Miyun Yuanwu rules it straight without bending and turns the proverb that plain speech beats a red face into its opposite; Hanxiu Ruqian opens an address to the garrison patrons with a great general taking the field, strike the head and the tail answers; Jifei Ruyi opens with the piled-up chain, trees into forest, days into years, good into success, merit into virtue, until doing-by-not-doing; Ruibai Mingxue answers the opening gavel of his inaugural seat with it: no one lacks it, no land fails to show it.
